Documents/Labtrac 2.9.5 upgrade — findin.summary: Labtrac 2.9.5 upgrade — findings from Arrowhead's rehearsal Arrowhead Dental Laboratory. Last updated 2026-09-23. This machine, Labtrac-Sandbox, rebuilds itself every night: it restores a fresh copy of our production Labtrac database and applies your 2.9.5 upgrade scripts to it. Everything below was found that way and can be reproduced here on request. Nothing here is inferred. Each item states what was run, what happened, and what closes it. See README - Labtrac Sandbox.md on this desktop for how the refresh works and how to run the steps by hand. Which scripts this is about The set you sent on 2026-09-21 as Newest Upgrade Scripts.zip. We accepted it as our standard set on 2026-09-22 after a full trial run, with the previous set armed as a per-script fallback. All 14 scripts ran, none failed, and nothing fell back — the drop is good. The items below are what remains. The scripts as we run them are on this machine in C:\temp\Labtrac\SQL Scripts. 1. 4 - Update Sp.sql cannot be applied to a 4229 database Three columns are read by the script and created by nothing in the set. ALTER PROCEDURE binds column names against tables that already exist, so this fails at install time, before any client application runs. Column Read by Error without it System_Log.OSVersion Labtrac_GetCurrentUsers Invalid column name 'OSVersion' System_Log.Permission Labtrac_GetCurrentUsers Invalid column name 'Permission' Surgeon_Summary.LastUpdate Surgeon_Update_Surgeon_Summary Invalid column name 'LastUpdate' Reproduced 2026-09-22 on a scratch database holding System_Log in its exact post-3 - Update Tables.sql shape, with ExeDate added but not OSVersion or Permission: TEST 1: create the proc with System_Log missing the two columns FAILED: Invalid column name 'OSVersion'. TEST 2: add the two columns, then try again CREATED OK TEST 3: same question for Surgeon_Summary.LastUpdate FAILED: Invalid column name 'LastUpdate'. None of the three exist on our 4229 production database. Checked with COL_LENGTH for all 30 columns we supply: 0 present, 30 absent. All 18 tables exist; only the columns are new. The client application does not create them. On 2026-09-23 we dropped System_Log.OSVersion and Tax_Area.DateCreated on this sandbox and logged in with the 2.9.5 client. The client wrote its System_Log row normally and both columns stayed absent. The client reads these columns; it does not create them. So they have to come from a script. To get the upgrade to complete, we add them ourselves at a fixed point in the sequence, immediately before 4 - Update Sp.sql. 2. Workbench task list returns HTTP 500 On a database upgraded strictly by the supplied scripts, the Workbench task list fails. GET /api/orgs/{org}/labs/{lab}/tasks -> 500 Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.SqlException (0x80131904): Invalid column name 'TimeStamp'. at Smilesolver.Workbench.LocalWorkbenchServices.ListAllTasksAsync(...) line 930 at Smilesolver.Workbench.Mvc.ApiControllers.TasksController.Get(...) line 24 Error Number: 207 The statement behind it, captured with Extended Events filtered on error 207: SELECT [p].[ID], [p].[Bonus], [p].[Deleted], [p].[Description], [p].[FixedPay], [p].[FixedUTA], [p].[LabID], [p].[LeadDays], [p].[MinDays], [p].[OutSourced], [p].[PreferredContractor], [p].[Sequence], [p].[SkillID], [p].[TimeStamp], [p].[UTA], [p].[UTADailyLimit], [p].[ValidForPay], [p].[WorkCenterID] FROM [Production_Steps] AS [p] WHERE [p].[Deleted] = CAST(0 AS bit) 3 - Update Tables.sql adds TimeStamp rowversion to 37 tables. Production_Steps is not one of them, and no supplied script mentions that table at all. Adding the column took the endpoint from 500 to 200 immediately, returning normal task data. We used your own pattern from 3 - Update Tables.sql: IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT * FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS WHERE TABLE_NAME = 'Production_Steps' AND COLUMN_NAME = 'TimeStamp') BEGIN ALTER TABLE [Production_Steps] ADD [TimeStamp] rowversion NOT NULL END; 3. Connected Users is always empty on 2.9.5 Labtrac_GetCurrentUsers filters on a fixed list of application names: WHERE SPR.program_name In ('Labtrac Desktop','Labtrac Enterprise', 'Labtrac Productivity Suite','Visual Basic') The 2.9.5 client connects as Labtrac 2.9.5.202, which is not in that list. The client's application name now carries the version; the procedure was not updated to match. Measured 2026-09-22 on both sides: Client identifies as Sessions matching the procedure's list Production, 4229 Labtrac Enterprise x141, Labtrac Productivity Suite x56 197 This sandbox, 2.9.5.202 Labtrac 2.9.5.202 0 This is not a sandbox artefact. Any customer on 2.9.5 will find Connected Users permanently empty. Clicking the username to view connected users also raises Invalid column name 'OSVersion' when item 1 is not addressed. 4. Three documented fixes have no corresponding script From the corrections list and release notes supplied 2026-09-22, each naming a database object: Change log entry State on our 4229 database In the script set "Lab_Delete_Lab_Inventory stored procedure added" exists, last modified 2012-06-05 not referenced "Order_insert_Order_stage_Enclosures SP updated to prevent multiple enclosures" exists, last modified 2012-06-05 not referenced "Removed recursion from Function RemoveBadSubContractorDateExt to prevent UI crash" does not exist not referenced 2 - Add Sp.sql is byte-identical to the previous set, so the two procedures above would still be running their 2012 definitions after the upgrade. 5. Open question — the other 26 columns Beyond the four that break something, 26 further columns exist in our upgraded reference and are created by no supplied script. They are DateCreated, LastUpdate and LabID columns across 17 tables. No supplied script reads or writes any of them, so nothing breaks without them — we add them only so the result matches the reference we were left with after the manual upgrade. Evidence that they belong to the upgrade rather than later drift: every one of their default constraints is timestamped 2025-09-02 15:09, the same window as the objects the scripts do create. Tables the application added afterwards — ManufactureOrder, OrderChat, WorkflowEvent — are dated 2025-09-08 through 2026-01-28 and are excluded. One detail may help identify the source: the DateCreated/LastUpdate defaults were explicitly named DF_<Table>_<Column>, in the style of your own DF_System_Log_ExeDate, while the LabID defaults were system-named. That suggests two different mechanisms, and that at least one of them came from a script we do not hold. What we are asking for The ALTER TABLE statements for the four columns that break the upgrade — the three in item 1 and Production_Steps.TimeStamp in item 2. Confirmation of whether the other 26 columns belong in 2.9.5. The scripts for the three objects in item 4, if those changes are meant to be in this release. A fix for the application-name filter in item 3. What the 2026-09-21 drop already fixed Worth saying plainly, because it was a real improvement on what we had: 1 - New Indexes.sql is now fully IF NOT EXISTS-guarded, and its two unguarded DROP INDEX statements are gone. 2 - Order_Stage_ClusteredPK.sql and A3 - Surgeon_ClusteredPK.sql use DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS. OPTIMIZE_FOR_SEQUENTIAL_KEY was removed from 4 - Product_Header_ClusteredPK.sql. Our production instance is SQL Server 2017, so that one mattered — the previous version could not run there at all. Seven documented changes map cleanly onto script changes: the Connect delete trigger, the Email_CaseEntrySource null-date fix, Order_Audit_Trail.Description widening to 250, the TrackingID audit entry, the duplicate user initials check, the Case Links character limit, and the parallel scheduling setting. Three script changes appear in neither document — the index guards, the DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS guards, and the OPTIMIZE_FOR_SEQUENTIAL_KEY removal. Those look like responses to what we reported rather than product changes, which would explain their absence from a product change log. One line of confirmation that they were deliberate would be helpful. Reproducing any of this The rehearsal runs nightly on this machine and can be run on demand. See README - Labtrac Sandbox.md on this desktop. The run record, including every script and how long it took, is at F:\SqlLanding\Status\LastRefresh.json.
